Netz HaChama (נץ החמה) is the halachic moment of sunrise. Different opinions compute it differently — based on whether the sun\'s center or upper limb crosses the horizon, whether atmospheric refraction is included, whether the observer is at sea level or elevated, and whether the eastern horizon is the geometric sea horizon or actual local terrain.
The three options in this app

Sea-level sunrise with atmospheric refraction, computed locally via the KosherJava library (NOAA solar algorithm). Equivalent to most published "sunrise" values for an observer at sea level. Same as Hebcal\'s "sunrise" field.

Visible sunrise from your elevation, looking out at a sea horizon. Earlier than Mishor when you\'re at altitude (KosherJava\'s getSunrise() with the device\'s GPS altitude). Important: this does NOT model the actual eastern terrain. It assumes the eastern horizon is the ocean — true for coastal observers, but inaccurate inland where mountains block the sun. For example, in Jerusalem the Mount of Olives delays the truly visible sunrise; this calculation does not account for that.

Sea-level sunrise fetched from hebcal.com\'s public Zmanim API. Numerically equivalent to local Mishor (Hebcal does not support elevation). Useful as a cross-check or for users who prefer matching what Hebcal publishes.
Why not the same as chaitables / printed luach?

Printed luchot from sources like חיים שכטר or לוחות חי use the actual eastern topographic horizon — the mountains, hills, or buildings that block the early sun. This is locality-specific data that we don\'t currently model on-device. A planned future option will let you upload a custom table for your locality so the countdown matches your local luach exactly.
Milestones must be in chronological order (higher offset first).
Invalid offset. Use MM:SS (seconds 0–59) or just minutes.
